title: Why One 30-Minute Meeting Wrecks a Whole Afternoon
alt_title_1: Paul Graham's Maker vs Manager Schedule Explained in 60 Seconds
alt_title_2: How to Protect 4-Hour Deep Focus Blocks From Calendar Creep
description_hook: In his classic 2009 essay 'Maker's Schedule, Manager's Schedule', Paul Graham explained why a single 30-minute afternoon meeting fractures four hours of creative output. Here is how to batch calls onto the edges of your day.

scenes.headline: How 30 Minutes Ruins a 4-Hour Afternoon
scenes.stat_label: ENOUGH TO FRACTURE AN ENTIRE MAKER AFTERNOON
bullets: Looks harmless on an hourly calendar grid
Splits deep focus into two unusable shards
scenes.narration: Why can a single thirty-minute check-in at two-thirty P.M. wipe out an entire four-hour afternoon of serious coding, writing, or strategy work?

scenes.headline: Paul Graham's Two Incompatible Clocks
bullets: Maker clock: half-day blocks needed to build complex work
scenes.narration: In his influential 2009 essay Maker's Schedule, Manager's Schedule, Y Combinator co-founder Paul Graham explained that workplaces run on two incompatible clocks: hourly manager slots versus half-day maker blocks.

scenes.headline: Midday Calls Split Context Into Fragments
scenes.left_body: Calls at 10:30 AM & 2:30 PM -> zero deep work finished
scenes.right_body: 8 AM-2 PM sealed focus -> all calls batched after 3:30 PM
scenes.narration: Managers switch tasks smoothly every sixty minutes. Makers must load complex mental models into working memory, so one mid-afternoon call splits a block into unusable fragments.

scenes.headline: Push Every Meeting to the Calendar's Edge
scenes.stat_subtext: Batch calls after 3:30 PM to preserve 4-hour creation blocks
scenes.narration: Protect deep output by clustering every call onto the edges of your day, after three-thirty P.M., leaving mornings and early afternoons completely unbroken.

scenes.headline: Defend Half-Day Blocks Like Client Calls
scenes.stat_label: MINIMUM UNIT OF SERIOUS CREATIVE CRAFT
bullets: Lock recurring morning maker blocks on your calendar
Stack calls back-to-back at the end of the afternoon
scenes.narration: Guard half-day maker blocks like client appointments, because finished assets only emerge inside long, quiet stretches.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin calendar protocol based on Paul Graham (2009)
